analysis.title: GS Tuteja - a bit less clear 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: The desk's late-August bullish view on AI and semis no longer has the same asymmetry. Macro is harder, and positioning in AI and large-cap tech is no longer a tailwind.

Since Aug 27, SPX is up 1.28% while SPXXAI (S&P ex the AI names) is down 5.19%. The rolling 30-day return gap between SPX and SPXXAI is near its widest since January 2023, and NDX vs RTY shows a similar split.
The largest SPX weights and parts of the AI trade have been immune so far to the sharp repricing in fixed income. That leaves them exposed to further negative macro surprises.
The desk sees two paths. Either rates and oil turn friendlier and the index rises on broader sector participation, or macro stays messy and large-cap tech and AI stall with the rest of the market.
The desk prefers broader-market upside structures to the AI ones it favored for the past few months. It cites SPXXAI Nov 102% calls for 1.25% as a convex right-tail hedge if macro turns friendlier.
US FCI has tightened about 40 bps since end of June, and SFRZ6Z7 has steepened almost 50 bps since end of August. The market is pricing more rate hikes through end of 2027.

Clients have re-engaged in tech. Mag7 is near 22% of total US net exposure on the GS prime book (highest since start of 2022), semis are about 12% (peak 14% in June, about 6% at start of year), and tech was the only sector net bought in September.

Long levered semis ETF AUM is about 115bln, against a June peak of about 157bln and a trough of about 72bln on 29 Jul. About 11bln of creations have come since the June peak. The desk does not see AI positioning at the June peak, but also no longer sees tech as under-owned.

Overall net positioning remains low. US Fundamental L/S nets sit in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback. The desk expects clients to add exposure on dips, and says about 7400 SPX is a level where they would meaningfully buy.

A real left tail in equities requires the Fed to hike an excessive number of times to protect credibility in back-end yields. CPI is the near-term risk. The October meeting is priced at 5 bps of hikes, and a high print that forces a hike would put downside on all sectors.

The desk's constructive Fed case is only a December hike followed by guidance toward quarterly hikes. Williams, Jefferson and Bowman introduced a data-dependent framework for the October meeting, which was met with optimism after the lighter NFP.

Middle Income Consumer (GSXUMIDC) and housing (GSXUHOME) have very low positioning and cheap multiples, but clients stay wary until macro clears. GSENEPOW (AI Power) has renewed client interest and clean positioning (15th percentile on a 3-year lookback), and the narrative is forming that midterms could clear policy uncertainty around datacenters.
The desk's year-end idea is to sell the 31Dec 85% put to fund a 110 135% call spread on GSENEPOW for 1.75%.
Global Fundamental L/S ended June at +17.42% and is now at +12.54%. SPX returns are seasonally flat from August to the midterms and fairly positive from the midterms to year-end.

GS estimated midterm implied moves. GSENEPOW has the largest extra midterm move at 1.69% (3.40% total vs 1.72% baseline), then GSTMTAIR at 1.49%, GSTMTAIP at 1.30%, and SPX at 0.31% (1.09% total vs 0.78% baseline).

The Fed having to hike an excessive number of times to maintain credibility in back-end bond yields.

tension_points.bull_case: Overall net positioning is very low (US Fundamental L/S in the 2nd percentile), multiples have compressed, and clients would buy dips near 7400. A data-dependent Fed and a path of only a December hike plus quarterly guidance could let equities react to dovish surprises. Cheap, under-owned pockets could broaden the rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro stays messy on rates and oil, and large-cap tech and AI, which were immune to the fixed income repricing, stall with the rest of the market. A high CPI print could force the Fed to hike in October and price much higher hikes for 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A high CPI print that forces the Fed to hike at the October meeting, which was priced at 5 bps of hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is not near the June peak (Mag7 at 22% of exposure, levered semis ETF AUM about 115bln vs about 157bln in June), so there is room before it becomes a headwind.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech and AI are no longer under-owned or priced to pessimism. Tech saw its largest monthly buying since Feb 25 in September, so the asymmetry has shifted and further negative macro surprises could hit these names.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tech and AI positioning has risen and macro is harder, so the upside asymmetry the desk saw in late August has shifted.
theme_stances.evidence: the Tech / AI asymmetry has shifted

theme_stances.key_argument: Unlocking real right tails in the broad SPX requires increased breadth into low-positioned, cheap-multiple parts of the market.
theme_stances.evidence: there needs to be increased market breadth

theme_stances.key_argument: A December-only hike with quarterly guidance would be positive for equities, while excessive hikes would open a left tail.
